# Adversarial Review Findings — Story 2.3 (Preiskategorie je Sitzplatz wählen)

- **No visual "needs a category" indicator on seats.** `seed-a-frontend/src/app/features/sitzplan/seat/seat.html` renders the identical `✓` / `.seat--selected` styling regardless of whether `categoryOf(seatId)` resolved a category or not. A mouse user can select several seats, click away from each panel before choosing a pill (nothing forces interaction with the panel), and end up with multiple "selected" seats that silently have no price category assigned — visually indistinguishable from seats that do. The only place this surfaces is the `aria-label` (screen readers only) or later, at booking time in Story 2.5.

- **`formatEuroAmount` has no thousands separator** (`seed-a-frontend/src/app/shared/format-currency.ts`): `amount.toFixed(2).replace('.', ',')` turns 1234.5 into `"1234,50 €"` instead of the German `"1.234,50 €"`. `Preis` is mapped as `decimal(10,2)` (up to 8 integer digits) with nothing in the DTO/entity/import path capping it below four digits, so the formatter's naive locale handling is one four-digit ticket price away from being visibly wrong.

- **No lower-bound validation on `Preis` anywhere in the pipeline** — `SeedPreiskategorie` (`seed-a-backend.Api/Data/Seed/SeedDatenbestand.cs`), `SeedImporter.cs`, the `PriceCategory` entity, and the EF Core `OnModelCreating` config all accept any decimal, including 0 or negative. A seed JSON entry missing `"preis"` silently defaults to `0m` (C# default) rather than failing the import — a category could quietly become free with no error raised.

- **No DB-level uniqueness constraint on `PriceCategories`** for `(EventId, Reihenfolge)` or `(EventId, Name)`. The `Reihenfolge` field's entire purpose (per the story's own comments) is to guarantee a stable, non-ambiguous display order, yet nothing in `AppDbContext.cs`/the migration actually enforces that two rows for the same event can't share an order index or name.

- **`PriceCategoryPanel`'s aria-label is static and seat-agnostic**: `role="group" aria-label="Preiskategorie wählen"` (`price-category-panel.html`) never references which seat the panel belongs to, unlike the carefully row/column-specific labels built for `<app-seat>` in the same feature. A screen-reader user who opens this panel for several different seats in one session hears the exact same context-free announcement every time.

- **No `aria-live` announcement when the panel appears.** A keyboard user who presses Enter/Space on a seat gets a new interactive panel rendered below the row with zero auditory cue that it exists — they have to already know to Tab forward to discover it. (Not contractually required by `EXPERIENCE.md`'s Accessibility Floor, which only mandates `aria-live="assertive"` for the FR-13 conflict banner, but it's an inconsistency given how deliberately a11y is handled everywhere else in this diff.)

- **The diff under review is missing `sitzplan-page.spec.ts`.** `git log --stat` on the actual commit shows 177 lines added to this file covering exactly the panel-open/pill-click/category-change/deselect/Escape/auto-assign/event-switch behaviors the acceptance criteria hinge on, but none of that is visible in the diff supplied for review — the file with the highest behavioral risk in this change (`sitzplan-page.ts`) is the one whose test evidence wasn't included for scrutiny. (Verified independently: the tests do exist and all 74 frontend / 21 backend tests pass, but that had to be checked out-of-band rather than read from the diff itself.)

- **`SeedPreiskategorie.Name` has no emptiness/length constraint**, and the mapped `PriceCategories.Name` column is `nvarchar(max)` with no `MaxLength`. An empty-string name imports cleanly and would render an anonymous pill ("· 32,00 €") with nothing anywhere to catch it.
